pages.title: The repetition code
pages.card: Flip qubits in a row, watch the parity checks between neighbours fire, and decode them, which on a line is a majority vote. Then simulate the logical error rate against the physical error rate for d = 1, 3, 5 and 7 and set it beside the exact curve.
Step through the encoder that spreads |0> over nine qubits and eight checks, then inject an X, Y or Z error on any qubit and see which checks fire and whether the readout survives.

pages.title: Errors, syndromes and decoding
pages.card: Place X, Z and Y errors on a d = 3, 5 or 7 patch and watch a union-find decoder grow clusters step by step. See how (d+1)/2 errors fool it, and why measurement errors need repeated rounds.

pages.title: The threshold
pages.card: Run Monte Carlo in the browser to draw the logical against the physical error rate for d = 3, 5, 7 and up and watch the curves cross. Read off the crossing and the suppression factor, switch on measurement errors, and compare with reference numbers from stim and pymatching.
Nine physical CNOTs between two patches act as one logical CNOT and leave a logical Bell pair. Then run the circuit live in the browser with your own noise level and an injected error.
Make the T state on one qubit with H and T, encode it as |T>_L, and compare the simulated readouts in X and Y with the ideal 14.6%.
Teleport |T>_L from patch A to patch C through a logical Bell pair on B and C, with a Pauli fix from the measured bits.

pages.title: Lattice surgery
pages.card: Merge two patches along an edge and split them again: the seam checks measure Z_L Z_L without reading either logical qubit. Step through it on 21 simulated qubits and run 200 shots.
